author: edwong57
body:
* **PTHR ID & PTN node:** *
PTHR11117 (Succinate/malate CoA ligase alpha subunit), PTN000122012. The IBA was made on 2026-05-28.
  with/from: RGD:619821, UniProtKB:O19069, UniProtKB:P0AGE9, UniProtKB:P53597, UniProtKB:Q51567,
  dictyBase:DDB_G0289325.

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**

  | UniProtKB | Gene (SGD) | IBA term |
  |---|---|---|
  | P53598 | LSC1 (YOR142W; SGD:S000005668) | GO:0004776 succinate-CoA ligase (GDP-forming) activity |

* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation, or other issue**

  **Erroneous propagation.**

  - PMID:9874242: "Genes of succinyl-CoA ligase from *Saccharomyces cerevisiae*". The yeast enzyme is ATP-specific.
    SGD annotates GO:0004775 *succinate-CoA ligase (ADP-forming) activity*.
  - UniProt names P53598 "Succinate--CoA ligase [ADP-forming] subunit alpha".

  - #1423 (closed 2017): the same wrong GDP-forming annotation on the *S. pombe* orthologue SPCC1620.08, which came in through EC2GO at the time. It cited the same yeast paper (PMID:9874242), and UniProt fixed it family-wide. Looks like the error has come back through a different route, the IBA from this node.

* Add the label 'high priority' if needed. Generally high priority issues affect a lot of proteins, and annotations are incorrect (as opposed to just imprecise).
title: PAINT issue: PTN000122012 (PTHR11117) propagates GDP-forming succinyl-CoA ligase to the yeast alpha subunit LSC1 (yeast enzyme is ADP-forming only)

author: marcfeuermann
body:
Thank you for reporting this issue. This is a somewhat unusual situation; most enzymes, from bacteria to vertebrates, catalyze both reactions. When we re-annotate trees after topology changes, it sometimes happens that we can no longer see what was done years ago. I reviewed the annotation and I especially created a **NOT** primary annotation for P53598 based on PMID:9874242. NOT annotations are not trivial, especially when there is evidence that a protein does not have the function one would expect it to have. They are extremely important for creating good models of function evolution with PAINT.
Also, most of annotations did not have the CONTRIBUTES_TO qualifier, so I also reviewed the whole annotation for this family.
The PAINTing looks a lot better now ;-)
Cheers,
Marc.
